shouldFix.title: g17Quoted.harnessVerbatim is a truncated prefix of the live cell, not the verbatim field
shouldFix.finding: The block quotes 'dropped / inapplicable (D-077 SARIF drop; D-086). not required-now.' The live DR-G17 harness cell reads 'dropped / inapplicable (D-077 SARIF drop; D-086). not required-now. advertised command/capability × canonical Run corpus × supported platform; V1 parity fixtures plus drop/change/truncation mutations'. The quotation stops at the first sentence boundary and the field is nonetheless labelled harnessVerbatim. The other four gate blocks — G19, G20, G21, G23 — are byte-exact on id, claim and harness, which is what makes this one stand out as carelessness rather than method.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: The omitted tail supports the artifact's own conclusion rather than cutting against it: 'advertised command/capability × canonical Run corpus × supported platform; V1 parity fixtures' is precisely a parity corpus over advertised surfaces, which is why NT-5's refuse-or-not-offer class cannot ride it. Nothing in the reasoning changes when the full cell is read.
shouldFix.repair: Quote the whole cell. If the intent was to show only the standing clause, add a separate field such as g17StandingClause and keep harnessVerbatim complete.

shouldFix.title: NT-4 carries a present-tense gate pair and execution-obligation owner that no instrument supports, and no owed naming act is recorded
shouldFix.finding: NT-4 is the one class marked capable-of-riding, with existingGate 'DR-G21 and DR-G23', existingHarness naming both harnesses, and executionObligationOwnerToday 'Supervisor + protocol + operability at G21; Protocol + semantic owners at G23'. Measured against every instrument that does naming: the live DR-G21 cell mentions neither DR-131 nor DR-133; the live DR-G23 cell names DR-133 NT-3 and NT-5 and not DR-131; and gate-harness-naming.v6, which is where class-level naming lives in this corpus, names DR-102's CC classes and DR-133's NT classes at G20 and G21, with its only DR-131 mention being 'Does not SATISFY DR-133, DR-131, or DR-117' in whatThisDoesNotDo. No DR-131 class is named at any gate. The artifact's substantive argument is coherent and I do not dispute it: v2's own pass sentence for NT-4 is 'Refused under DR-133', so executing DR-133 NT-1, NT-2 and NT-3 exercises that refusal and the class adds no new obligation. But the fields assert something different from that argument — an existing gate pair and an owner today — and the two cannot both be right. The DR-133 family shows what the honest handling looks like: provider-only-nt-gate-join.v6 marked its riding classes capable-of-riding and recorded an owedLater D-086 successor, which D-145 and D-147 then performed by writing the class names into the gate entries. This artifact records no owedLater at all. A later DR-131 cycle asking whether NT-4's remainder is already named at a condition-4 obligation with an owner would be pointed at two gates that do not name it.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing false about readiness follows today. Seven of eight classes are leftover regardless, so gates 2 and 3 fail on those alone; the artifact says so, adds no row, and moves no cardinality. The defect is a present-tense claim in one class entry, not a wrong bottom line.
shouldFix.repair: Pick the reading and make the fields match it. If NT-4 is genuinely not a distinct test because its pass is DR-133's pass, set existingGate and executionObligationOwnerToday to none and say the remainder is discharged by DR-133's named classes at G21 and G23, citing D-145 and D-147 — that keeps leftoverDesign false honestly. If instead DR-131 NT-4 must itself be named for gate 3 purposes, keep capable-of-riding and add an owedLater block for a D-086 successor that names DR-131 NT-4 at those gates, exactly as join v6 did for DR-133.

independence.priorParticipation: I reviewed every step of the DR-133 chain whose form this artifact pins, and the D-147 act that created the DR-G23 row it invokes. The risk is grading a familiar shape by recognition. So I re-measured the predecessor's application, read all five invoked gate rows in full from the post-D-147 file, compared all twenty-four NT fields against the contract, and checked the naming state in both file 08 and the naming artifact rather than assuming the DR-133 pattern carried over to DR-131.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX. Twelve attacks run, two landed. Custody is clean: 5ee2bb3e at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left e68cc88, file 08 at the 23cdf039 pin the artifact itself carries, governing tree clean. I verified the predecessor act first, since this artifact reasons over a file 08 that D-147 rewrote: the applied DR-G23 row and the applied condition-4 cell are byte-identical to the blocks consented at D-147 turn 2, condition 4 is still MET, and the 65 non-gate rows are untouched. On the substance the artifact is conservative and, on my own measurement, right. All twenty-four NT verbatim fields across the eight classes are byte-exact against preview-analyze-contract.v2, the DR-131 evidence cell is byte-exact, and four of the five gate blocks are byte-exact on id, claim and harness. The seven leftover verdicts hold: I read all five invoked gate rows in full and none owns pack-identity admission, imperative-pack IR, missing-rung Coverage typing, analyze SARIF advertisement, sealed-Run labelling, host verdict minting or host D9 minting. The reasons distinguish near neighbours precisely, including that DR-133 NT-4 at G20 is component-set policy while DR-131 NT-7 is host-side derivation — a different actor. No row is proposed, required-now stays 19, and nothing retargets the DR-133 namings. Two narrow things block. First, g17Quoted.harnessVerbatim is a truncated prefix: the live cell continues 'advertised command/capability × canonical Run corpus × supported platform; V1 parity fixtures plus drop/change/truncation mutations', and a field labelled verbatim must carry the field. The omitted tail actually supports the artifact's own conclusion, which makes it carelessness rather than selection, and the other four blocks show the method is otherwise sound. Second, NT-4 carries existingGate 'DR-G21 and DR-G23' and an execution-obligation owner today, and no instrument supports that: the live G21 cell mentions neither DR-131 nor DR-133, the live G23 cell names DR-133 NT-3 and NT-5 only, and gate-harness-naming.v6's sole DR-131 mention is the line saying it does not SATISFY DR-131. The artifact's argument — that v2's own pass for NT-4 is 'Refused under DR-133', so DR-133's named classes exercise it and no new obligation arises — is coherent and I do not dispute it; the fields simply assert a different thing. The DR-133 family shows both honest options, and the join it pins as form recorded an owedLater for exactly this situation while this one records none. Either set NT-4's gate and owner to none and say the remainder is discharged by DR-133's named classes at G21 and G23 under D-145 and D-147, or keep capable-of-riding and record the owed D-086 successor that would name DR-131 NT-4 there.
